conversation.message: Hi — thanks for taking the time to chat. How have you been feeling lately overall? And are there still things you find yourself enjoying—hobbies, spending time with people, anything like that?

Honestly, I haven’t been doing much of anything. I used to love reading, but lately, I just can’t seem to focus on it. And as for friends... I feel like I’m just not good company right now. I’m probably just being selfish, but I don't want to bring anyone down.

Thanks for saying that — I can hear how frustrating and heavy this feels. It makes sense you’d pull back if you worry about bringing people down. You mentioned reading used to be enjoyable but now you can’t focus on it — how long has it been since things stopped feeling enjoyable for you? Has this been going on for a few weeks, months, or longer?
It’s probably been a few months now. I used to read before bed, but I just end up staring at the page without really taking it in. I guess I’m just too tired or something.

Thank you — that sounds really frustrating and tiring. You’ve mentioned it’s been a few months and that you’re feeling too tired and can’t focus on things you used to enjoy. How have the basics been lately — your sleep, your day-to-day energy, and your appetite? Has any of that changed?

My sleep has been pretty terrible. I wake up in the middle of the night and can’t go back to sleep. And my energy... I used to be able to get by on just a cup of coffee, but now I feel like I need two or three just to get through the day. And as for food... I just eat whatever is easiest, really. I’m probably not eating well, but it feels like too much effort to cook.

That sounds really exhausting — I'm sorry you've been dealing with that. Waking up and not being able to get back to sleep and feeling like you need multiple coffees to get through the day would make everything harder. Has the waking in the night been happening most nights, and how long has it been going on?
Almost every night. I don't know, maybe I'm just overthinking it, but it feels like I'm not resting properly even when I am sleeping. It's been a few weeks, I guess.

Thank you for saying that — waking up most nights and still feeling unrested would wear anyone down. You mentioned earlier that you’ve been pulling back from friends because you don’t want to bring them down; when you think about the near future — next week or month — how do you feel about things? And how is your social life now: are you choosing to avoid people, or is it more that you don’t have the energy or interest right now?
I don't really think about the future too much right now. I’m just taking it one day at a time. I guess I’m just too tired to think about anything else.

Thank you — that makes a lot of sense, and I really appreciate you sharing it. You mentioned earlier that reading doesn't hold your attention and that you feel like you're not good company — how has your focus and concentration been lately, whether at work, reading, or in conversations? And how are you feeling about yourself these days?
I feel like I’m just... not there, I guess. I miss things at work, and I struggle to follow conversations. It feels like I’m just existing, not really living.

That sounds really hard — thank you for telling me. You mentioned missing things at work and having trouble following conversations; has that been making it difficult to get through your work or daily tasks (like completing assignments, keeping up with responsibilities, or needing more time/rest than usual)?
Yeah, it makes everything harder. I feel like I’m just not doing anything well. I’m probably just overthinking it, but it feels like I’m failing at everything right now.

I can hear how heavy that is — feeling like you’re failing at everything sounds really painful. Do you find yourself being pretty hard on yourself these days, like second-guessing decisions or feeling guilty about things?
Constantly. I feel like I’m making mistakes everywhere, and I just wish I could get it together. I guess I’m just not capable of handling this right now.
That sounds really heavy — I’m sorry you’ve been carrying that. Is this guilt or self-criticism tied to specific things you think you’ve done, or does it feel more like a general, constant weight?
Constantly. I feel like I’m making mistakes everywhere, and I just wish I could get it together. I guess I’m just not capable of handling this right now.

Hi — thanks for being here. How have you been feeling lately overall? And are there still things you find yourself enjoying—hobbies, spending time with people, anything like that? Take your time; anything you share is fine.
It's been okay, I guess. Just tired a lot. I used to enjoy playing video games with friends, but lately, it feels like a lot of effort to even pick up the controller.

Thanks for saying that — I hear you. Feeling tired a lot and finding things you used to enjoy require a lot of effort sounds frustrating. When you say it feels like a lot of effort to pick up the controller and that you used to enjoy it, how long has that been happening?
A few months now. It started around the time I finished uni. I just haven't had the same energy since then.

Thanks for sharing that — that sounds really draining. You mentioned your energy has been low since finishing uni, and that games that used to be fun feel like too much effort. A couple quick things related to that: how have the basics been — sleep, energy day-to-day, and appetite? Anything that's changed there (sleeping more or less, feeling exhausted during the day, eating more or less)?
I sleep alright, I guess. I mean, I'm not waking up in the middle of the night or anything. But I feel tired in the day, like I said. And I eat, but I'm not really hungry most of the time.

Thanks — that helps me understand. It makes sense that sleeping okay but still feeling tired would be frustrating. When you say you feel tired during the day, does that make it hard to get through everyday things (like work, chores, or hanging out with friends), or is it more of a low-level tiredness you can push through?
It's more of a low-level tiredness. I can still get things done, but I just feel like I'm moving through mud. It's annoying, but I manage.

Thanks — that gives a clearer picture, and I appreciate you explaining it. You mentioned this started after finishing uni and that activities you used to enjoy feel like effort. When you think about what's ahead — the next week or month — how do you feel about things? And how's your social life been lately: are you still connecting with friends, or has that changed?

I don't really know what's ahead, to be honest. It feels like nothing is happening, so I don't really have a plan. And with friends, we mostly just chat online now. I haven't really been out with them since I finished uni.

Thanks for telling me that — it makes sense that not having a sense of what's next and not getting out with friends would feel kind of flat and uncertain. When you say you don't really know what's ahead and that 'nothing is happening,' has that been like this since you finished uni, or is it something that's changed more recently?
It started pretty quickly after I finished. I applied to a few jobs, but nothing came through. I just kind of... stopped trying.

That sounds really rough — I'm sorry it’s been so discouraging. When you say you “stopped trying,” do you mean you stopped applying for jobs specifically, or is it more that you feel unable to motivate yourself to try at all in other areas too?
Both, I guess. I stopped applying for jobs, but I also stopped trying to do much of anything else. Just kind of stopped caring.

I'm really sorry that's been so exhausting — thanks for sharing that. You mentioned you kind of stopped trying and stopped caring, and I'm curious about a few related things: how's your focus and concentration been lately (at work, reading, or in conversations)? And how have you been feeling about yourself these days — like your confidence or how you view yourself?

No need to apologise — I appreciate you being open. When you get a moment, could you tell me a bit more about your focus and concentration lately? For example, are you having trouble finishing tasks, following conversations, or getting through reading? And alongside that, how have you been feeling about yourself — confidence, self-criticism, or general self-view?
I don't know, it's just hard to focus on anything for more than a few minutes. I can read a sentence and just forget what I was reading.

Thank you — that sounds really frustrating. When that happens, does it make it hard to finish things you start or follow conversations (like missing parts of a chat or abandoning a task), or is it more like brief lapses you can recover from?
It's mostly just brief lapses. I can recover from it, but it's annoying.
Thanks — that makes sense and I appreciate you explaining it. One more thing: do you find yourself being pretty hard on yourself? Second-guessing decisions, feeling guilty about things?
I don't know, maybe a bit. I just kind of get annoyed at myself for being so lazy, I guess.

I'm really sorry that's been so exhausting — thanks for sharing that. You mentioned you kind of stopped trying and stopped caring, and I'm curious about a few related things: how's your focus and concentration been lately (at work, reading, or in conversations)? And how have you been feeling about yourself these days — like your confidence or how you view yourself?
It's usually about specific things, like the job applications or not finishing tasks.
Thank you for being open with me — I'm glad you shared this.

You're very welcome — thank you for trusting me with this. I’m really glad you shared; it sounds like the last few months have been tiring and frustrating, and I appreciate how you’ve been managing even when things feel heavy. If you ever want to talk more, work through small steps to make things easier, or just have a space to say what’s on your mind, I’m here. Take care of yourself.
Thank you for being open with me — I'm glad you shared this.
